meta.note: Adjectives and adverbs of daily life.

cards.note: Adjective 'good' — pairs with nouns: um café bom. Feminine is irregular: boa. For 'well' with verbs use bem, never bom.
cards.ex_t: Este bolo do caco é mesmo bom.
cards.ex_trans: This bolo do caco is really good.

cards.note: Adverb 'well' — pairs with verbs: correu bem, falas bem. Also intensifies: bem cedo = quite early. Never swap with the adjective bom.
cards.ex_t: Correu tudo bem na AIMA, já tenho a morada atualizada.
cards.ex_trans: Everything went well at AIMA, my address is already updated.

cards.note: Adjective 'bad' — mau tempo. Feminine is irregular: má. The adverb is mal.
cards.ex_t: O tempo está mau no norte da ilha hoje.
cards.ex_trans: The weather is bad in the north of the island today.

cards.note: Adverb 'badly' — dormi mal. Also 'hardly / as soon as': mal cheguei. Not the adjective mau.
cards.ex_t: Sem café, trabalho mal a manhã toda.
cards.ex_trans: Without coffee I work badly all morning.

cards.note: One form for both genders. After the noun = big (uma casa grande); before it = great (um grande amigo).
cards.ex_t: Leva uma garrafa de água grande para a levada.
cards.ex_trans: Take a big bottle of water for the levada.

cards.note: In Portugal breakfast is o pequeno-almoço — 'café da manhã' is Brazilian.
cards.ex_t: O nosso apartamento é pequeno, mas tem varanda.
cards.ex_trans: Our flat is small, but it has a balcony.

cards.note: Also means 'young': o colega novo can be the young colleague. Context decides.
cards.ex_t: Comprei um telemóvel novo na Worten.
cards.ex_trans: I bought a new mobile phone at Worten.

cards.note: Fine for things; for people mais velho or idoso is politer.
cards.ex_t: O prédio é velho, mas o elevador funciona bem.
cards.ex_trans: The building is old, but the lift works well.

cards.note: Everyday speech in Portugal often prefers giro/gira for 'pretty, cute'.
cards.ex_t: O pôr do sol na Ponta do Sol é muito bonito.
cards.ex_trans: The sunset at Ponta do Sol is very beautiful.

cards.note: Same form for m/f; plural fáceis.
cards.ex_t: A levada dos Balcões é fácil, dá para ir com crianças.
cards.ex_trans: The Balcões levada is easy, you can go with kids.

cards.ex_t: É difícil encontrar estacionamento no centro do Funchal.
cards.ex_trans: It's difficult to find parking in central Funchal.

cards.note: Adjective; as an everyday adverb Portugal prefers depressa: fala depressa.
cards.ex_t: O teleférico é mais rápido do que o autocarro para o Monte.
cards.ex_trans: The cable car is faster than the bus to Monte.

cards.note: ch sounds like English 'sh'. cheio de = full of; estou cheio = I'm full (food).
cards.ex_t: O autocarro das oito está sempre cheio.
cards.ex_trans: The eight o'clock bus is always full.

cards.ex_t: O quarto já está limpo, podes entrar.
cards.ex_trans: The room is already clean, you can go in.

cards.ex_t: O chão do mercado fica sujo ao fim do dia.
cards.ex_trans: The market floor gets dirty by the end of the day.

cards.note: 'You are right' is tens razão, not 'estás certo'. Certo? at the end of a sentence = right?/agreed?
cards.ex_t: Desta vez apanhei o autocarro certo.
cards.ex_trans: This time I caught the right bus.

cards.note: Takes a: igual ao teu, igual à minha — never 'igual que'. Same form for m/f.
cards.ex_t: A poncha aqui é igual à do Funchal, mas mais barata.
cards.ex_trans: The poncha here is the same as in Funchal, but cheaper.

cards.note: Takes de: diferente do Funchal. Same form for m/f.
cards.ex_t: O clima no norte é bem diferente do clima no Funchal.
cards.ex_trans: The climate in the north is quite different from the climate in Funchal.

cards.ex_t: É importante guardar o recibo da renda.
cards.ex_trans: It's important to keep the rent receipt.

cards.note: With estar: estou cansado = I'm tired. 'Tiring' is cansativo — o dia foi cansativo.
cards.ex_t: Estou cansado, a levada do Caldeirão Verde é longa.
cards.ex_trans: I'm tired, the Caldeirão Verde levada is long.

cards.note: Same form for m/f; used with estar for a momentary 'pleased'.
cards.ex_t: Estou contente com o apartamento novo no Caniço.
cards.ex_trans: I'm pleased with the new flat in Caniço.

cards.note: Same form for m/f; plural felizes. Stronger and more lasting than contente, which is the everyday 'glad'.
cards.ex_t: O vizinho está feliz porque o Marítimo ganhou.
cards.ex_trans: The neighbour is happy because Marítimo won.

cards.note: Adjective, agrees: sozinha. The adverb só also means 'alone', but sozinho is more common.
cards.ex_t: Não vás sozinho à levada, o tempo muda depressa.
cards.ex_trans: Don't go on the levada alone, the weather changes fast.

cards.note: Usually plural and agrees in gender: duas colegas vão juntas.
cards.ex_t: Vamos juntos ao mercado no sábado de manhã.
cards.ex_trans: Let's go to the market together on Saturday morning.

cards.note: Invariable before adjectives and adverbs: muito cansada. Agrees before nouns: muitas pessoas.
cards.ex_t: Hoje está muito calor no Funchal.
cards.ex_trans: It's very hot in Funchal today.

cards.note: Same rule as muito: pouco simpática (invariable) vs poucas lojas (agrees). um pouco = a bit.
cards.ex_t: Há pouco estacionamento perto do mercado.
cards.ex_trans: There's little parking near the market.

cards.note: Means 'quite / plenty of', not English 'enough' — that is suficiente, or chega ('that's enough').
cards.ex_t: A subida para o Monte é bastante íngreme.
cards.ex_trans: The climb up to Monte is quite steep.

cards.note: The pt-PT word for 'too': demasiado caro. Brazilians say muito caro or caro demais — you will rarely hear demasiado in Brazil.
cards.ex_t: Esse restaurante na marina é demasiado caro.
cards.ex_trans: That restaurant at the marina is too expensive.

cards.ex_t: O frigorífico está quase vazio, temos de ir ao Pingo Doce.
cards.ex_trans: The fridge is almost empty, we have to go to Pingo Doce.

cards.note: Wider than 'already': já vou = I'm coming right now; Já foste à Calheta? = Have you ever been...; já não = not anymore (not 'not yet').
cards.ex_t: Já tens o cartão de residência da AIMA?
cards.ex_trans: Do you already have the residence card from AIMA?

cards.note: 'Still' in positives: ainda trabalho lá. With não it means 'not yet': ainda não. Opposite of já não = no longer.
cards.ex_t: Ainda estou à espera do técnico da MEO.
cards.ex_trans: I'm still waiting for the MEO technician.

cards.note: In negatives use também não: Eu também não = me neither.
cards.ex_t: Eu também trabalho a partir de casa às sextas.
cards.ex_trans: I also work from home on Fridays.

cards.note: Also 'alone' (estou só). Apenas is the formal synonym; só is what you hear in daily life.
cards.ex_t: Só tenho uma nota de vinte, tens troco?
cards.ex_trans: I only have a twenty note, do you have change?

cards.note: antes de + infinitive: antes de sair = before leaving.
cards.ex_t: Vê a previsão do tempo antes de fazer a levada.
cards.ex_trans: Check the weather forecast before doing the levada.

cards.note: depois de + infinitive: depois de almoçar. Alone = afterwards.
cards.ex_t: Vamos beber uma poncha depois do trabalho.
cards.ex_trans: Let's have a poncha after work.
